claim: The government is entitled to permissive intervention under Rule 24(b) where the same facts underlie both the civil and criminal actions, but a blanket stay of civil discovery pending parallel criminal proceedings is not warranted, except that a defendant facing criminal trial may not be deposed in order to preserve his right to avoid self-incrimination or an adverse inference, and a defendant who has already pled guilty is not entitled to a stay of civil proceedings on self-incrimination grounds as his guilty plea estops him from contesting the civil allegations.
initial_reasoning: The cited opinion (97 F. Supp. 3d 558) grants the government permissive intervention under Rule 24(b) because the civil and criminal actions share the same facts, denies a blanket stay of discovery while staying only the deposition of the criminal defendant, and holds that a defendant who has pleaded guilty is estopped from invoking self‑incrimination to halt civil proceedings. These holdings directly correspond to each element of the claim.
